text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar softened to 475.25/475.60 per dollar, traders said, although it may firm again later in the week as portfolio inflows to the Caracas stock exchange make themselves felt in the exchange rate.
On Friday the unit closed at 475.00/475.50 per dollar.
"The supply of dollars we saw last week has dried-up somewhat," said one trader. "But it could well begin again...there's alot of foreign money flowing into the bolsa."
Traders said the Central Bank provided the market with dollars in the late afternoon after a slow start to the session.
Banks tightened buy/sell spreads "to increase their competitiveness amid today's light trade," said one trader.
